ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r4.claim: God tolerates arrogance and disorder only while expedient, then destroys those whose collective existence threatens the world; Thamūd exemplify the warning to Quraysh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p329/r4.anchor: When these things cross the bounds, the Almighty destroys them and cleanses His world from people whose existence becomes dangerous for it in their collective capacity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p330/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p330/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p330/r1.claim: The Quraysh are warned that if they adopt Thamūd’s arrogant attitude, God will seize them and no one can help.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p330/r1.anchor: no one would be able to help them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r4.claim: Nations are punished collectively in this world for collective rebellion, while each person is individually judged and rewarded or punished in the Hereafter.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r4.anchor: In the Hereafter, each person will be held accountable in his personal capacity

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r5.claim: Historical evidence shows that a rebellious nation is given time and a clear warning, then destroyed if it persists in denial without excuse.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p336/r5.anchor: it is communicated the truth to the extent that it is left with no excuse to deny the truth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r1.claim: Cosmic and inward evidence mainly serves reflective intellectuals; historical incidents can move ordinary people who are able to learn from them, so the Qur’an uses both forms of proof.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r1.anchor: evidence from incidents and events are more effective

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r2.claim: The Qur’an mentions Thamūd alone here, although it names many nations elsewhere; its history was especially familiar to the Quraysh.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r2.anchor: has mentioned many nations to highlight this aspect

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r3.claim: Islahi quotes his mentor Imām Farāhī: Quraysh knew the Thamūd’s history, and the Qur’anic allusion was enough to evoke the whole account, including their inherited settlements and traditions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r3.anchor: has discussed their history and their resemblance

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r4.claim: The brief Qur’anic account could evoke the Thamūd’s full fate for the Quraysh because their history was familiar and often discussed among them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r4.anchor: was enough to point to their complete history

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p337/r5.claim: A cited Arabic couplet treats Qidār as a figure overcome by time, evidence that Thamūd were known in Arab poetry.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p338/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p338/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p338/r1.claim: Qidār, who killed the she-camel, was an autocratic and rebellious Thamūd leader, comparable to Qayl ibn ʿUmar of ʿĀd.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p338/r1.anchor: He was an autocratic and rebellious leader

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p338/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p338/r2.speaker: al-Afwah al-Awdī
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p338/r2.claim: Al-Afwah compares his nation’s corrupt elements to Qayl and Qidār, portraying them as destructive, resistant to guidance, and driven by folly and rebellion.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r1.claim: Thamūd’s rebellion, leaders’ deviance, and fate were proverbial among Arabs, so the Qur’an’s short reference conveyed a full history to its first audience.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r1.anchor: so well known to the Arabs

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r5.claim: After Ṣāliḥ warned them, Thamūd demanded a sign; he made the she-camel both a sign of punishment and a test with an assigned drinking turn.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r5.anchor: nominated a she-camel as a sign for this punishment

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p339/r6.claim: After Thamūd hamstrung the camel, God gave them three days to repent; the respite increased their arrogance, and punishment destroyed them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r2.claim: Thamūd ignored this last warning just as they had rejected the earlier threat, dismissing it as intimidation and pressure.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r2.anchor: mere intimidation and a pressure tactic

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r3.claim: ʿAqr literally means hamstringing a camel; since that causes certain death, killing is an implied, resultant sense rather than the primary meaning.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r4.claim: Although one person killed the camel, God attributes the crime and punishment to the whole nation because it sanctioned the act; only those who tried to reform him or dissociated themselves were spared.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r4.anchor: one person was responsible for killing the she-camel

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r5.claim: Damdamah denotes killing with great intensity; Islahi renders it a resounding punishment and connects it to the scourge described elsewhere.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r5.anchor: very appropriate for such a punishment

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r6.claim: The severe punishment fits the camel’s role as a sign and trial of the nation’s rebellion; God punished them for harming it despite warnings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p340/r6.anchor: punishment was meted out to them

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p341/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p341/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p341/r1.claim: The camel tested the whole nation’s rebellion; further respite might have led them to kill the Messenger, a crime that always brings a nation’s destruction.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p341/r1.anchor: whenever a nation planned to kill its Messenger, it was necessarily destroyed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p341/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p341/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p341/r2.claim: Islahi suggests the sūrah came while Quraysh leaders secretly plotted Muhammad’s killing at Dār al-Nadwah; it alludes to consequences and urges reflection.

QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r8.claim: The most wretched among them killed the she-camel; Salih warned them to leave God's camel and its drinking share alone.
QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r8.anchor: عاقرها . { فقال لهم رسول الله ناقة الله وسقياها } . أي : احذروا ناقة الله

QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r9.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r9.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r9.claim: God destroyed the people for their crime and leveled them; another explanation says all shared the same punishment because they approved the camel's slaughter.
QUSHAYRI:v3p424/r9.anchor: سوى بينهم ربهم في العذاب لأنهم كلهم رضوا بعقر الناقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p484/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p484/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p484/r6.claim: Damdam عليه can mean the grave covered him; Muraij explains it as total destruction, while al-Ṣiḥāḥ glosses it as pressing and crushing something against the earth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p484/r6.anchor: دمدم عليه القبر: أطبقه. وقال مؤرج: الدمدمة:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r1.claim: The majority say Thamūd were unbelievers; a report says they had followed Ṣāliḥ for a time, then disbelieved and hamstrung the camel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r1.anchor: وروي أنهم كانوا قد أسلموا قبل ذلك وتابعوا صالحا بمدة، ثم كذبوا وعقروا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r2.claim: The whole community is charged with hamstringing the camel because its members approved and conspired in the act.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r2.anchor: وأسند العقر للجماعة لكونهم راضين به ومتمالئين عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r3.speaker: ابن الزبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reads fa-dahdama with an inserted hāʾ, meaning that the punishment was repeatedly brought down upon them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r3.anchor: وابن الزبير: فدهدم بهاء بينهما، أي أطبق عليهم العذاب مكررا ذلك عليهم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r4.claim: The phrase بذنبهم warns of the consequences of sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r4.anchor: بذنبهم: فيه تخويف من عاقبة الذنوب، فسواها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r5.claim: One interpretation says the tribe was made equal in destruction; another says the punishment was distributed evenly and spared neither young nor old.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p490/r5.anchor: قيل: فسوى القبيلة في الهلاك، عاد عليها بالتأنيث كما عاد في بطغواها. وقيل: سوى الدمدمة، أي سواها بينهم،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r11.claim: The oath answer is that God will devastate Mecca for rejecting the Messenger, as He devastated Thamud for rejecting Salih; قد أفلح is a digression continuing the preceding point, not the oath answer.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p762/r11.anchor: على أهل مكة لتكذيبهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r7.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r7.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r7.claim: The creator first emerges through indirect, enigmatic mā in the second half of the series; the explicit naming of the Lord in verse 14 resolves the suspense.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:1-8:kommentar/r7.anchor: Das dadurch aufgebaute Spannungsmoment löst im Grunde erst die explizite Nennung des „Herrn“ in V. 14 auf

BURSEVI:v10p345/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p345/r6.speaker: السهيلي
BURSEVI:v10p345/r6.claim: Al-Suhayli names Qudar ibn Salif as the killer, Qadira as his mother, and Musda ibn Wihrawa ibn Jahm as his accomplice.
BURSEVI:v10p345/r6.anchor: قال السهيلي العاقر قدار بن سالف وأمه قديرة وصاحبه الذي شاركه في عقر الناقة

BURSEVI:v10p345/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p345/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p345/r9.claim: Damdam means to enclose and cover completely; repeating د intensifies the encompassing, as shown by the sequence دممت ثم دمدمت in Kashf al-Asrar.
BURSEVI:v10p345/r9.anchor: فأطبق عليم العذاب وهو الصيحة الهائلة

BURSEVI:v10p345/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p345/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p345/r10.claim: The phrase because of their sin explicitly warns every sinner; leveling them means none escaped, young or old, or that Thamud were flattened to the ground.
BURSEVI:v10p345/r10.anchor: والتصريح بذلك مع دلالة الفاء عليه للإنذار بعاقبة الذنب ليعتبر به كل مذنب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r4.claim: If the success statement is parenthetical, the story's consequence of Thamūd's destruction answers the oath; its lām is omitted to shorten an already long oath, as in Sūrat al-Burūj.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r4.anchor: ولام الجواب محذوف تخفيفا لاستطالة القسم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r5.claim: The oath indirectly threatens the arrogant Quraysh, who resemble Thamūd in knowingly rejecting the Messenger; God swears they will suffer a like punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r5.anchor: التعريض بتهديد المشركين الذين كذبوا الرسول طغيانا هم يعلمونه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r6.claim: The Meccans had experienced the sword's punishment at the hands of enemies after persecuting and expelling the Prophet, a particularly bitter chastisement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p371/r6.anchor: ولقد أصاب المشركين عذاب السيف بأيدي الذين عادوهم وآذوهم وأخرجوهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r8.claim: The later 'they denied him' means they rejected the warning and its threatened punishment; thus the she-camel sign followed an earlier rejection, as in the account in Sūrat Hūd.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p372/r8.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أن آية الناقة أرسلت لهم بعد أن كذبوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r1.claim: Alternatively, the fa merely introduces details after a general statement, as in other Quranic examples; Thamūd denied through arrogance when their most wicked man rose, with the warning and hamstringing then elaborating the episode.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الفاء للترتيب الذكري المجرد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r2.claim: Plural pronouns are used because Thamūd are a people collectively, although the earlier reference treats Thamūd grammatically as a tribe name.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r2.anchor: وأعيدت عليهم ضمائر الجمع باعتبار أنهم جمع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r7.claim: The denial following the warning is a second denial: they rejected the threat implied by the prohibition, as stated explicitly in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p373/r7.anchor: والتكذيب المعقب به تحذيره إياهم بقوله : { ناقة الله } ، تكذيب ثانن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r1.claim: ʿAqr is wounding a camel's forelegs so pain makes it kneel for slaughter at the breast; because the acts are connected, the word conventionally implies slaughter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r1.anchor: جرح البعير في يديه ليبرك على الأرض من الألم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r2.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr reads damdama as God's angry shout, the sound of the lightning and quake that destroyed them; its attribution to God is figurative because He creates the sound and its qualities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r2.anchor: والمراد بهذه الدمدمة صوت الصاعقة والرجفة التي أهلكوا بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r3.claim: Most commentators instead interpret damdama as covering them with the earth, from the verb damm for covering a grave; reduplication intensifies the meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r3.anchor: وقال أكثر المفسرين : دمدم عليهم أطبق عليهم الأرض

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r4.claim: On Ibn ʿĀshūr's reading, sawāhā means the punishment struck them evenly; its feminine pronoun refers to the dundering/punishment understood from damdama.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r5.claim: Those who take damdama as burying them understand sawāhā to mean the earth became level over them, hiding their bodies and dwellings; its pronoun then refers to the implicit earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r5.anchor: جعل الأرض مستوية عليهم لا تظهر فيها أجسادهم ولا بلادهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r6.claim: The phrase fa-sawwāhā forms complete paronomasia with wa-mā sawwāhā earlier in the same surah.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p374/r6.anchor: وبين { فسواها } هنا وقوله : { وما سواها } ( الشمس : 7 ) قبله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r18.claim: The command about God's she-camel and her drink has an omitted verb such as preserve, leave, or beware of violating her right; the camel story is treated in other surahs.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p488/r18.anchor: ناقة الله وسقياها نصب بفعل مضمر تقديره احفظوا أو ذروا أو احذروا على معنى: احذروا الإخلال بحق ذلك،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p489/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p489/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p489/r2.claim: Damdama means sending down punishment that unsettles them repeatedly; manuscript or reader variants include fahadhdama, fadammara, and a reading attributed to Ibn Masud.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p489/r2.anchor: «دمدم» معناه: أنزل العقاب مقلقا لهم مكررا ذلك وهي الدمدمة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p489/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p489/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p489/r3.claim: Bi-dhanbihim means because of their sin; fasawwāhā means the whole tribe was leveled in destruction and none survived.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p489/r3.anchor:
بذنبهم أي بسبب ذنبهم، وقوله تعالى:
فسواها، معناه: فسوى القبيلة في الهلاك لم ينج منهم أحد،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r1.claim: They disbelieved Ṣāliḥ's warning that slaughtering the camel would bring punishment, then hamstrung it; damdama means enveloping them with punishment, or destroying them utterly.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r1.anchor: ﴿ فكذبوه ﴾ في تحذيره إياهم العذاب بعقرها ﴿ فعقروها ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains damdama as enclosing them with punishment, repeating the covering until complete.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r2.anchor: فدمدم عليهم ربهم قال الزجاج أي أطبق عليهم العذاب يقال دمدمت على الشيء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r3.speaker: المؤرج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r3.claim: Al-Muʾarrij says damdama means total destruction.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r4.speaker: السدي ويحيى بن سلام
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r4.claim: One view says God leveled them together in destruction, killing young and old alike.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r4.anchor: أحدهما سوى بينهم في الإهلاك قاله السدي ويحيى بن سلام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r5.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r5.claim: A second view says God leveled their houses over their graves; they had dug graves and lain in them, and after the cry killed them their houses fell upon the graves.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p143/r5.anchor: والثاني سوى الأرض عليهم قال مقاتل سوى بيوتهم على قبورهم

IBNKATHIR:91:14/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:14/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:91:14/r1.claim: Thamud rejected Salih's message and hamstrung the she-camel, which God had brought from the rock as a sign and proof against them.
IBNKATHIR:91:14/r1.anchor: كذبوه فيما جاءهم به فأعقبهم ذلك أن عقروا الناقة التي أخرجها الله من الصخرة آية لهم وحجة عليهم

IBNKATHIR:91:14/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:14/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:91:14/r2.claim: Damdama means that God became angry with them and destroyed them; fasawwaha means that He leveled the punishment over them alike.
IBNKATHIR:91:14/r2.anchor: أي : غضب عليهم ،   فدمر عليهم ،   { فَسَوَّاهَا } أي : فجعل العقوبة نازلة عليهم على السواء .

IBNKATHIR:91:14/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:91:14/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR:91:14/r3.claim: Qatada reports that the camel-killer waited until young and old, men and women, followed him; because the people shared in killing her, God destroyed all of them for their sins.
IBNKATHIR:91:14/r3.anchor: قال قتادة : بلغنا أن أحيمر ثمود لم يعقر الناقة حتى تابعه صغيرهم وكبيرهم ،   وذكرهم وأنثاهم ،

FARRA:v3p269/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p269/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p269/r1.claim: The sequence “they denied him, then hamstrung her” can mean their killing the messenger itself was sufficient proof of denial.
FARRA:v3p269/r1.anchor: على ما ظن، لأنك تقول: قتلوا رسولهم فكذبوه، أي: كفى بالقتل تكذيبا،

FARRA:v3p269/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p269/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p269/r2.claim: Alternatively, “they denied him” is complete by itself and “they hamstrung her” answers the earlier “when its most wretched one arose.”
FARRA:v3p269/r2.anchor:
ويكون فكذبوه كلمة مكتفى بها، ويكون قوله:
(فعقروها) جوابا لقوله: (إذ انبعث أشقاها)

FARRA:v3p269/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p269/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p269/r3.claim: The verbs may be fronted or delayed because hamstringing was the denial, and the acts occurred together; their order can vary.
FARRA:v3p269/r3.anchor: ويكون مقدما ومؤخرا لأن العقر وقع بالتكذيب، وإذا وقع الفعلان معا جاز تقديم أيهما شئت.

FARRA:v3p269/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p269/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p269/r4.claim: They had agreed to the she-camel’s allotted drinking day without believing the agreement.
FARRA:v3p269/r4.anchor: ولهم شرب فجاء في التفسير: أنهم كانوا أقروا بهذا غير مصدقين له:

FARRA:v3p269/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p269/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p269/r5.claim: Damdam means he devastated them; “made it even” can mean he treated the nation alike, striking both young and old.
FARRA:v3p269/r5.anchor:
بهم. «فسواها» (14) عليهم.
ويقال: فسواها: سوى الأمة، أنزل العذاب بصغيرها وكبيرها

JISHUMI:v10p7434/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r3.speaker: ابن زبير
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r3.claim: He reads فدهدم instead of the common فدمدم; the author says only the established widespread form may be recited.
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r3.anchor: وعن ابن زبير: (فدهدم) وقد تبدل الهاء بالميم

JISHUMI:v10p7434/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r8.claim: ʿAqr originally means cutting into an animal's body, spilling blood, and removing flesh.
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r8.anchor: والعقر: أصله نقض شيء من بنية الحيوان، عقره يعقره

JISHUMI:v10p7434/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r9.claim: Damdama is the repeated infliction of an unpleasant, intensified hardship, like the doubled forms dam and ṣarṣar.
JISHUMI:v10p7434/r9.anchor: والدمدمة: ترديد الحال المتكرهة، وهي مضاعفة لما فيه من المشقة

KASHSHAF:91:14/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:14/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:14/r1.claim: They denied the warning that punishment would descend if they acted, then hamstrung the she-camel.
KASHSHAF:91:14/r1.anchor: فيما حذرهم منه من نزول العذاب إن فعلوا

KASHSHAF:91:14/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:14/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:14/r2.claim: Damdama means to unleash punishment, related to the expression for a camel coated with fat.
KASHSHAF:91:14/r2.anchor: فأطلق عليهم العذاب ،   وهو من تكرير قولهم

KASHSHAF:91:14/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:14/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:14/r3.claim: Their fate gives a grave warning about sin and calls every sinner to take heed.
KASHSHAF:91:14/r3.anchor: بسبب ذنبهم .   وفيه إنذار عظيم بعاقبه الذنب

KASHSHAF:91:14/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:91:14/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:91:14/r4.claim: The final pronoun refers to the punishment: it leveled them all, sparing neither young nor old.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r8.claim: They rejected the warning that punishment would descend; dammadama means punishment overwhelmed them, and their sin warns others to beware sin.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r8.anchor: { فكذبوه } فيما حذرهم منه من نزول العذاب إن فعلوا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r9.claim: Fa-sawwaha may refer to the punishment, which leveled them all, or to Thamud, leveled to earth or destroyed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p764#2/r9.anchor: الضمير للدمدمة ، أي : فسواها بينهم لم يفلت منها صغيرهم

MAWARDI:91:14/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:14/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI:91:14/r1.claim: Dammadama has three interpretations: God became angry with them, encompassed them, or destroyed them; the word is also known in Abyssinian.
MAWARDI:91:14/r1.anchor: فيه ثلاثة أوجه : أحدها : معناه فغضب عليهم . الثاني : معناه فأطبق عليهم . الثالث : معناه فدمّر عليهم

MAWARDI:91:14/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:14/r2.speaker: السدي ويحيى بن سلام
MAWARDI:91:14/r2.claim: Al-Suddi and Yahya ibn Sallam say God made them equal in destruction.
MAWARDI:91:14/r2.anchor: أحدهما : فسوى بينهم في الهلاك ، قاله السدي ويحيى بن سلام

MAWARDI:91:14/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:14/r3.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI:91:14/r3.claim: Ibn Shajara interprets the phrase as leveling them into the earth.
MAWARDI:91:14/r3.anchor: الثاني : فسوّى بهم الأرض ، ذكره ابن شجرة

MAWARDI:91:14/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:91:14/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI:91:14/r4.claim: A further possibility is that God made later nations equal to them.
MAWARDI:91:14/r4.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثاً : فسوّى مَن بعدهم مِنَ الأمم

MUQATIL:91:14-15/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:91:14-15/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:91:14-15/r1.claim: After the she-camel was killed, her calf fled up a mountain and cried three times that its mother had been killed; the people asked Ṣāliḥ what to do, but the calf escaped when they tried to seize it.
MUQATIL:91:14-15/r1.anchor: لما عقروا الناقة ابتعد الفصيل حتى صعد على جبل فصاح ثلاث مرات: يا صالح، قتلت أمى

MUQATIL:91:14-15/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:91:14-15/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:91:14-15/r2.claim: Ṣāliḥ said the three cries gave the people three days: their faces would turn yellow, then red, then black, before punishment on the fourth. They prepared graves, embalmed themselves, and at first mistook the delay for mercy.
MUQATIL:91:14-15/r2.anchor: تمتعوا في داركم ثلاثة أيام ذلك الوعد الذي صاح الفصيل غير مكذوب

MUQATIL:91:14-15/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:91:14-15/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:91:14-15/r3.claim: On the fourth day Gabriel blocked the sunlight; people fled back to their graves, and Gabriel's cry caused their souls to leave their bodies while their houses collapsed onto their graves, leaving the town as if it had never existed.
MUQATIL:91:14-15/r3.anchor: فصاح بهم جبريل صيحة أن قوموا عليكم لعنة الله، فسالت أرواحهم من أجسادهم

MUQATIL:91:14-15/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:91:14-15/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:91:14-15/r4.claim: To have God bring down the destruction for their sin and level it means their houses were leveled onto their graves.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#8/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#8/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#8/r1.claim: They denied Salih's warning of punishment and hamstrung the she-camel; the act is attributed to all because they approved it, as in the cited account of their calling their accomplice.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#8/r1.anchor: أى الناقة اسند الفعل اليهم وان كان العاقر واحدا لقوله فنادوا صاحبهم فتعاطى فعقر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#8/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#8/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#8/r2.claim: God annihilated them completely for their denial and hamstringing, making the destruction equal across them so neither child nor adult escaped.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p342#8/r2.anchor: ﴿ فدمدم عليهم ربهم ﴾ أهلكهم هلاك استئصال ﴿ بذنبهم ﴾ بسبب ذنبهم

QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari infers that God will destroy Meccans for denying Muhammad as He destroyed Thamud for denying Salih; verses 9–10 are an aside, not the oath’s answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:9-10/r3.anchor: الزمخشري: تقديره ليدمدمن الله عليهم أي على أهل مكة، لتكذيبهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، كما دمدم على ثمود لأنهم كذبوا صالحا

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r6.claim: They denied Salih’s warning that they would be punished if they hamstrung the camel.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r6.anchor: { فكذبوه } أي كذبوا صالحا عليه السلام في قوله لهم

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r7.claim: One man hamstrung the camel, but the deed is attributed to all because they approved it.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r7.anchor: { فعقروها } أي عقرها الأشقى. وأضيف إلى الكل، لأنهم رضوا بفعله

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r8.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r8.claim: Qatada says the killer did not act until all the people, young and old, men and women, followed him.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة: ذكر لنا أنه لم يعقرها حتى تابعه صغيرهم وكبيرهم، وذكرهم وأنثاهم

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r9.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r9.claim: Al-Farra says two men killed her; Arabic can use a plural praise or superlative for two, explaining the singular “most wretched.”
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r9.anchor: وقال الفراء: عقرها اثنان: والعرب تقول: هذان أفضل الناس، وهذان خير الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r10.claim: God destroyed them for their guilt: unbelief, denial, and hamstringing the camel.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r10.anchor: أي أهلكهم وأطبق عليهم العذاب بذنبهم الذي هو الكفر والتكذيب والعقر

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas, through al-Dahhak, glosses damdama as destroying them for their crime.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r11.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال: دمدم عليهم قال: دمر عليهم ربهم بذنبهم أي بجرمهم

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r12.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r12.claim: Al-Farra says damdama means shaking or making quake.

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r13.claim: Damdama literally intensifies and repeats punishment; damma means enclosing or sealing, and repetition expresses total destruction.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r13.anchor: وحقيقة الدمدمة تضعيف العذاب وترديده. ويقال: دممت على الشيء: أي أطبقت عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r14.speaker: المؤرج
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r14.claim: Al-Muarrij defines damdama as annihilation and extermination.

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r15.claim: A lexicon says damdama can mean sticking something to the earth and crushing it; God’s damdama means destroying them.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r15.anchor: وفي الصحاح: ودمدمت الشيء: إذا ألزقته بالأرض وطحطحته. ودمدم الله عليهم: أي أهلكهم

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r16.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r16.claim: Al-Qushayri cites the sense of covering a dead person with earth; God destroyed them by putting them beneath the ground.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r16.anchor: القشيري: وقيل دمدمت على الميت التراب: أي سويت عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r17.claim: Fasawaha can mean leveling the earth over them or making destruction fall evenly on the whole people.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r17.anchor: { فسواها } أي سوى عليهم الأرض. وعلى الأول «فسواها» أي فسوى الدمدمة

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r18.speaker: ابن الأنباري
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r18.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says damdama means anger; some linguists also use it for sustained action, as with a fat camel.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r18.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: دمدم أي غضب. والدمدمة: الكلام الذي يزعج الرجل

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r19.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r19.claim: Another explanation says punishment was equal across the people, young and old, poor and noble, men and women.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r19.anchor: وقيل: «فسواها» أي فسوى الأمة في إنزال العذاب بهم

QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r20.speaker: ابن الزبير
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r20.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reads fahadham, a dialectal variant like imtaqa/intaqa.
QURTUBI-FULL:91:13-14/r20.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير «فدهدم» وهما، لغتان كما يقال امتقع لونه وانتقع

NAHHAS:v5p237/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p237/r11.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p237/r11.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes the sequence to mean they slaughtered her and thereby lied to him.

NAHHAS:v5p237/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p237/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p237/r12.claim: The author rejects that reversal because fa marks a second event after the first, and no such reading is necessary: they called Ṣāliḥ a liar about the threatened punishment, then slaughtered the she-camel.
NAHHAS:v5p237/r12.anchor: وهذا خطأ في الفاء لأنها تدل على أن ثانيا بعد الأول وهذا عكس اللغة

NAHHAS:v5p237/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p237/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p237/r13.claim: Alternatively, fakadhdhabūhu is complete before fa-ʿaqarūhā is coordinated.
NAHHAS:v5p237/r13.anchor: وقد قيل فكذبوه كلام تام ثم عطف عليه فعقروها

NAHHAS:v5p237/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p237/r14.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p237/r14.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the people acknowledged the she-camel's arrangement but did not truly believe.
NAHHAS:v5p237/r14.anchor: فزعم الفراء أن الجواب عن هذا أنهم أقروا به ولم يؤمنوا

NAHHAS:v5p237/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p237/r15.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p237/r15.claim: The author rejects that unseen claim as requiring transmitted evidence and says the existing report contradicts it.
NAHHAS:v5p237/r15.anchor: وهذا القول الذي قاله مما لا يجب أن يجترأ عليه إلا برواية لأنه مغيب والرواية بخلافه

NAHHAS:v5p237/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p237/r16.speaker: قتادة
NAHHAS:v5p237/r16.claim: Qatāda reports that Qudār held back until the entire people, young and old, men and women, joined in denying Ṣāliḥ; this explains the universal punishment.
NAHHAS:v5p237/r16.anchor: روى سعيد عن قتادة قال توقف أحيمر ثمود عن عقر الناقة حتى اجتمعوا كلهم معه على تكذيب صالح

NAHHAS:v5p237/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p237/r17.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p237/r17.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses fa-damdama as shaking or quaking.

NAHHAS:v5p237/r18.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p237/r18.speaker: غيره
NAHHAS:v5p237/r18.claim: Another interpreter glosses fa-damdama as punished them.

NAHHAS:v5p237/r19.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p237/r19.speaker: علي بن سليمان
NAHHAS:v5p237/r19.claim: ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān says the pronoun in fa-sawwāhā returns to the implied damdamah.
NAHHAS:v5p237/r19.anchor: قال أبو جعفر سألت علي بن سليمان عن هذا الضمير فقال يعود على الدمدمة

NAHHAS:v5p237/r20.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p237/r20.speaker: غيره
NAHHAS:v5p237/r20.claim: Another explanation is that God made them equal in punishment and destroyed them all.
NAHHAS:v5p237/r20.anchor: وقال غيره أي سوى بينهم في العقوبة فأهلكهم جميعا

QUTB-ZILAL:91:14/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:14/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:14/r1.claim: Though one man hamstrung the camel, the whole people shared responsibility because they approved his act and did not stop him; this is a central Islamic principle of shared social accountability.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:14/r1.anchor: ولكنهم جميعا حملوا التبعة وعدوا أنهم عقروها ، لأنهم لم يضربوا على يده

QUTB-ZILAL:91:14/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:14/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:14/r2.claim: Collective responsibility in this life does not erase individual responsibility for the afterlife; neglecting mutual counsel, urging good, and restraining wrongdoing is itself culpable.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:14/r2.anchor: لا يتعارض مع التبعة الفردية في الجزاء الأخروي حيث لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى

QUTB-ZILAL:91:14/r3.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:14/r3.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:14/r3.claim: Damdam means divine wrath and the punishment following it; the word's sound evokes and pictures a terrifying scene.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:14/r3.anchor: واللفظ ذاته . . ( دمدم )يوحي بما وراءه ، ويصور معناه بجرسه

QUTB-ZILAL:91:14/r4.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:91:14/r4.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:91:14/r4.claim: God devastated the land, leveling its upper and lower parts in a scene of violent destruction.
QUTB-ZILAL:91:14/r4.anchor: وقد سوى الله أرضهم عاليها بسافلها ، وهو المشهد الذي يرتسم بعد الدمار العنيف الشديد

RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r1.claim: The warning of punishment did not prevent Thamud from denying Salih or hamstringing the she-camel.
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r1.anchor: لم يمتنعوا عن تكذيب صالح ، وعن عقر الناقة

RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r2.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r2.claim: The act can be attributed to one direct perpetrator, Qudar, or to the whole people for approving it; Qatada reports that everyone pledged before the deed, as most exegetes say.
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r2.anchor: قال قتادة : ذكر لنا أنه أبى أن يعقرها حتى بايعه صغيرهم

RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r3.claim: Al-Farra says the camel's killers were two men.
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء : قيل إنهما كانا إثنين

RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r4.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says damdama means covering them with punishment, enveloping them from every side.
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج : معنى دمدم أطبق عليهم العذاب

RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r5.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r5.claim: Al-Wahidi connects damdama with staining or coating something with fat, yielding punishment smeared all around them.
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r5.anchor: قال الواحدي : الدم في اللغة اللطخ

RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r6.claim: A second reading of damdama is burying or leveling them beneath the earth.

RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r7.speaker: ابن الأنباري
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r7.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says damdama means anger or disturbing speech.

RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r8.speaker: ثعلب عن ابن الأعرابي
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r8.claim: Thaʿlab transmits from Ibn al-Aʿrabi that damdama means shaking the earth over them; al-Farra adopts this view.

RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r9.claim: If damdama means enveloping punishment, 'made it even' means Gabriel's cry killed everyone alike; if it means leveling, God flattened the earth over them.
RAZI-FULL:v31p177#3/r9.anchor: وذلك أن هلاكهم كان بصيحة جبريل عليه السلام

SAMIN-DURR:91:14/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:14/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:91:14/r1.claim: Damdama is variously glossed as covering or enclosing, pressing to the ground, utterly destroying, imitating the sound of a collapse, or coating cloth with dye.
SAMIN-DURR:91:14/r1.anchor: الدمدمة. قيل: الإطباق يقال: دمدمت عليه القبر، أي: أطبقته عليه. وقيل: الإلزاق بالأرض

SAMIN-DURR:91:14/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:14/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:91:14/r2.claim: The bāʾ in bi-dhanbihim marks cause.

SAMIN-DURR:91:14/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:14/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:91:14/r3.claim: In fa-sawwāhā, the object pronoun can refer to Thamūd as a tribe, or to the punishment, leveled among them so none escaped.
SAMIN-DURR:91:14/r3.anchor: الضمير المنصوب يجوز عوده على ثمود باعتبار القبيلة كما أعاده في قوله " بطغواها

SAMIN-DURR:91:14/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:91:14/r4.speaker: ابن الزبير
SAMIN-DURR:91:14/r4.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr reads fa-dahdama with hāʾ instead of mīm; it has the same meaning as the common reading.
SAMIN-DURR:91:14/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن الزبير " فدهدم " بهاء بين الدالين بدل الميم، وهي بمعنى القراءة المشهورة

STUDYQURAN:91:11/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r4.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r4.claim: The Prophet identified those who hamstrung the she-camel as the most wretched people of earlier generations.
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r4.anchor: It is recorded that the Prophet said that the most wretched of previous generations

STUDYQURAN:91:11/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r5.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r5.claim: Some interpret ʿaqqarūhā as saying that they slaughtered the she-camel.
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r5.anchor: Some interpret hamstrung her (ʿaqqarūhā) as “slaughtered her”

STUDYQURAN:91:11/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r6.claim: Damdama describes an exceptionally severe punishment that came suddenly and annihilated and entirely covered the people.
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r6.anchor: indicates the most severe of punishments

STUDYQURAN:91:11/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r7.claim: Sawwāhā can mean God razed their city or leveled the earth over them, or distributed the same punishment to every tribe member.
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r7.anchor: It could also be rendered, “He distributed it equally,” meaning that God distributed the same punishment upon every member of the tribe

STUDYQURAN:91:11/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r8.claim: Using sawwā for both human creation and destruction suggests God destroys as easily as He creates and that punishment continues His fashioning of the soul.
STUDYQURAN:91:11/r8.anchor: The use of sawwā in this context, in relation to both the creation of human beings in v. 7 and their destruction in v. 14

TAB-FULL:v24p449#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p449#3/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p449#3/r1.claim: Their denial concerned Ṣāliḥ's warning that killing the camel would bring God's punishment; 6:4 also describes Thamūd and ʿĀd as denying the overwhelming event.
TAB-FULL:v24p449#3/r1.anchor: وقد كان القوم قبل قتل الناقة مسلمين، لها شرب يوم، ولهم شرب يوم آخر. قيل: جاء الخبر أنهم بعد تسليمهم ذلك، أجمعوا على منعها الشرب

TAB-FULL:v24p449#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p449#3/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p449#3/r2.claim: Ṭabarī allows that the denial may instead refer to the killing itself, since denial and killing can be ordered either way when closely linked as cause and act.
TAB-FULL:v24p449#3/r2.anchor: وقد زعم بعضهم أن قوله: {فكذبوه} [الأعراف: 64] كلمة مكتفية بنفسها، وأن قوله: {فعقروها} [هود: 65] جواب لقوله: {إذ انبعث أشقاها}

TAB-FULL:v24p449#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p449#3/r3.speaker: بعض أهل العربية
TAB-FULL:v24p449#3/r3.claim: Some grammarians treat 'they denied him' as a complete clause and make the killing answer the clause about the most wretched man rising.
TAB-FULL:v24p449#3/r3.anchor: وقد زعم بعضهم أن قوله: {فكذبوه} [الأعراف: 64] كلمة مكتفية بنفسها، وأن قوله: {فعقروها} [هود: 65] جواب لقوله

TAB-FULL:v24p449#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p449#3/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p449#3/r4.claim: Although the people had accepted the camel's alternating water days, they collectively agreed to stop her drink and accepted her slaughter, so denial and killing are attributed to all.
TAB-FULL:v24p449#3/r4.anchor: أجمعوا على منعها الشرب، ورضوا بقتلها، وعن رضا جميعهم قتلها قاتلها، وعقرها من عقرها

TAB-FULL:v24p451/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p451/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p451/r1.claim: God destroyed all of Thamūd for their sin, disbelief, denial of Ṣāliḥ, and slaughter of the camel; none escaped the punishment.
TAB-FULL:v24p451/r1.anchor: فلما اشترك القوم في عقرها دمدم الله عليهم بذنبهم فسواها

TAB-FULL:v24p451/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p451/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p451/r2.claim: Qatāda reports that every age and both sexes of Thamūd agreed with the killer before he slaughtered the camel, so all shared the punishment.
TAB-FULL:v24p451/r2.anchor: حتى بايعه صغيرهم وكبيرهم، وذكرهم وأنثاهم، فلما اشترك القوم في عقرها

TAB-FULL:v24p451/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p451/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v24p451/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says that when Thamūd sought the camel's calf, it fled to a mountain cleft, and God cut their hearts.
TAB-FULL:v24p451/r3.anchor: لما عقروا الناقة طلبوا فصيلها، فصار في قارة الجبل، فقطع الله قلوبهم

TABATABAI:91:11-15/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r5.claim: They denied Ṣāliḥ and hamstrung the camel; dammadma means an encompassing punishment that cuts off and erases their trace for their sin.
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r5.anchor: والدمدمة على الشيء الإطباق عليه يقال دمدم عليه القبر أي أطبقه عليه

TABATABAI:91:11-15/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r6.claim: The pronoun in “leveled it” most likely refers to Thamūd, leveled with the earth, or to the flattened land; another view takes it as the catastrophe, made equal so no one escaped.
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r6.anchor: الظاهر أن الضمير لثمود باعتبار أنهم قبيلة أي فسواها بالأرض

TABATABAI:91:11-15/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r7.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r7.claim: An alternative reads the pronoun as the punishment, which struck all alike so that none escaped, strong or weak, old or young.
TABATABAI:91:11-15/r7.anchor: وقيل الضمير للدمدمة المفهومة من قوله { فدمدم } والمعنى فسوى الدمدمة بينهم

ZAJJAJ:v5p333/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p333/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p333/r2.claim: They disbelieved the warning and did not believe punishment would come when told not to harm the she-camel.
ZAJJAJ:v5p333/r2.anchor: أي فلم يوقنوا أنهم يعذبون حين قال لهم (ولا تمسوها بسوء فيأخذكم عذاب يوم عظيم).

ZAJJAJ:v5p333/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p333/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p333/r3.claim: Damdama means to cover or encompass with punishment; repeated application intensifies the covering, as in covering a grave or a camel coated in fat.
ZAJJAJ:v5p333/r3.anchor:
معناه دمدم عليهم أطبق عليهم العذاب، يقال: دمدمت على الشيء إذا
أطبقت عليه،

TABRISI:91:14/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:91:14/r10.claim: Ṭughwā and ṭughyān denote going beyond the limit in corruption; some read bi-ṭughwā with a ḍamma as a verbal noun.
TABRISI:91:14/r10.anchor: والطغوى والطغيان مجاوزة الحد في الفساد وبلوغ غايته

TABRISI:91:14/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14/r11.speaker: الحسن، حماد بن مسلمة
TABRISI:91:14/r11.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Ḥammād b. Maslama read bi-ṭughwā with ḍamma as a feminine verbal noun like rajʿā and ḥusnā.
TABRISI:91:14/r11.anchor: وفي قراءة الحسن وحماد بن مسلمة بطغويها بضم الطاء

TABRISI:91:14/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:91:14/r14.claim: ʿAqr is cutting flesh so blood flows, and can mean damage at an animal's root, by analogy with a basin's base.
TABRISI:91:14/r14.anchor: والعقر قطع اللحم بما يسيل الدم وهو من عقر الحوض أي أصله

TABRISI:91:14/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14/r15.speaker: مؤرج، ابن الأعرابي
TABRISI:91:14/r15.claim: Mūʿarij says damdama is devastating repeated hardship; Ibn al-Aʿrābī says it is complete punishment.
TABRISI:91:14/r15.anchor: والدمدمة ترديد الحال المستكره وهي مضاعفة ما فيه الشقة

TABRISI:91:14/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14/r16.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
TABRISI:91:14/r16.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī also glosses damdama as fully punishing.
TABRISI:91:14/r16.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: دمدم أي عذب عذابا تاما

TABRISI:91:14-15/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14-15/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:91:14-15/r5.claim: Ṣāliḥ's people rejected him and his warning, then slaughtered the she-camel.
TABRISI:91:14-15/r5.anchor: أي فكذب قوم صالح صالحا ولم يلتفتوا إلى قوله وتحذيره إياهم

TABRISI:91:14-15/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14-15/r6.speaker: عطاء، مقاتل
TABRISI:91:14-15/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and Muqātil gloss damdama as God destroying them.
TABRISI:91:14-15/r6.anchor: أي فدمر عليهم ربهم عن عطاء ومقاتل

TABRISI:91:14-15/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14-15/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:91:14-15/r7.claim: Another explanation says God covered them with punishment and destroyed them.

TABRISI:91:14-15/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14-15/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:91:14-15/r8.claim: All were liable because they approved and urged the slaughter and had demanded the sign; their rebellion earned total destruction.
TABRISI:91:14-15/r8.anchor: لأنهم رضوا جميعا به وحثوا عليه وكانوا قد اقترحوا تلك الآية

TABRISI:91:14-15/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14-15/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:91:14-15/r9.claim: God made the punishment encompass the whole people, young and old, with no one escaping.
TABRISI:91:14-15/r9.anchor: فسوى الدمدمة عليهم وعمهم بها فاستوت على صغيرهم وكبيرهم ولم يفلت منها أحد منهم

TABRISI:91:14-15/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14-15/r10.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:91:14-15/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says God made the community equal by punishing its young and old alike.
TABRISI:91:14-15/r10.anchor: سوى الأمة أي أنزل العذاب بصغيرها وكبيرها فسوى بينها فيه عن الفراء

TABRISI:91:14-15/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:91:14-15/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:91:14-15/r11.claim: Other explanations say God flattened people uniformly into the earth or leveled their land over them.
TABRISI:91:14-15/r11.anchor: جعل بعضها على مقدار بعض في الاندكاك واللصوق بالأرض

ASAD-NOTES:91:11#n9/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:91:11#n9/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:91:11#n9/r1.claim: Asad refers to his note on 7:91 for his rendering of aqaruha.
ASAD-NOTES:91:11#n9/r1.anchor: For this rendering of aqaruha, see note 61 on 7:91

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r1.claim: They denied Ṣāliḥ's warning of punishment for hamstringing the camel; the accusative “God's she-camel” itself signals warning.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r1.anchor: {فكذبوه} أي بتحذيره إياهم العذاب بعقرها، وذلك أن قوله: {ناقة الله}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r2.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ's report, damdama means that God destroyed them; Muqātil gives a similar gloss.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r2.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: فدمر عليهم ربهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r3.speaker: المؤرج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r3.claim: Damdama means annihilation that leaves nothing behind.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r4.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r4.anchor: وقال ابن الأعرابي: دمدم: إذا عذب عذابا تاما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r5.claim: Damdama means enclosing them in punishment, as one covers or layers something; repetition intensifies the sense of covering.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r5.anchor: وذكر الزجاج: أصل هذا الحرف، فقال: معنى دمدم: أطبق عليهم العذاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r6.claim: Damdama may mean leveling the earth over them and burying them; fasawwāhā supports this, and Ibn ʿAbbās glosses it as leveling the earth over them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r6.anchor: فيجوز أن يكون معنى "فدمدم عليهم" سوي عليهم الأرض

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r7.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r7.claim: If damdama means enveloping punishment, fasawwāhā means the affliction covered them all equally: Gabriel's blast killed young and old alike.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r7.anchor: وتلك الصيحة أهلكتهم جميعا فاستوت على صغيرهم، وكبيرهم، (قاله مقاتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r8.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r8.claim: Damdama can mean anger, or disturbing speech that agitates a person.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r8.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري: دمدم: غضب قال وتكون الدمدمة الكلام الذي يزعج الرجل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r9.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r9.claim: Most commentators say the earth shook violently over them; Thaʿlab's report from Ibn al-Aʿrābī and al-Farrāʾ give the same gloss.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p68/r9.anchor: المفسرين قالوا في: {فدمدم عليهم}: أرجف الأرض بهم

WAHIDI-QT:91:14/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:91:14/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:91:14/r1.claim: They rejected Salih and killed the camel; God utterly destroyed them, making the destruction encompass them all.
WAHIDI-QT:91:14/r1.anchor: { فكذبوه فعقروها } فقتلوا الناقة { فدمدم عليهم ربهم } أهلكهم هلاك استئصال { بذنبهم فسواها } سوى الدمدمة عليهم فعمهم بها

WAHIDI-QT:91:14/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:91:14/r2.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-QT:91:14/r2.claim: Another view says God leveled Thamud through destruction, bringing it upon young and old alike.
WAHIDI-QT:91:14/r2.anchor: وقيل سوى ثمود بالهلاك فأنزله بصغيرها وكبيرها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r6.claim: They denied Salih and killed the camel; God utterly destroyed them for their sin and leveled the punishment over them all.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r6.anchor: فكذبوه فعقروها } فقتلوا الناقة { فدمدم عليهم ربهم } أهلكهم هلاك استئصال { بذنبهم فسواها }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r7.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r7.claim: Another explanation says God leveled Thamud through destruction, afflicting young and old alike.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:91:9-15/r7.anchor: وقيل: سوى ثمود بالهلاك، فأنزله بصغيرها وكبيرها.

ELMALILI:91:11-15/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r8.claim: The worst offender and his accomplices, and by extension the whole people, disbelieved Salih's warning and slaughtered the she-camel.
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r8.anchor: fakat o eşkā ve maiyyeti ve dolayısıyla o kavim o Allah’ın resûlünü tekzib ettiler

ELMALILI:91:11-15/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r9.claim: Aqr originally means cutting an animal's legs and tendons to kill it.
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r9.anchor: bir hayvanın ayaklarını biçip yıkarak öldürmektir.

ELMALILI:91:11-15/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r10.claim: Damdama means pressing wrath and applying punishment; related passages describe a cry, earthquake, or humiliating thunderbolt that struck them down and destroyed them.
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r10.anchor: Hışmını bası basıverdi, azâbını tatbik ediverdi

ELMALILI:91:11-15/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r11.claim: God made the punishment even across all who rejected Salih, including those who shared by silence and their families, destroying them utterly; alternatively, He levelled the earth over them, reversing the earlier fashioning.
ELMALILI:91:11-15/r11.anchor: o azâbı yalnız en şakīlerine ve bilfiil onun maiyyetinde bulunanlara değil, Sâlih’e iman etmeyen

ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r1.claim: Demdeme is the reduplicated form of damma: repeated smearing or coating that surrounds and forcefully covers its object.
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r1.anchor: “Demdeme” beyan olunduğuna göre دَمَّ fiilinden mükerrerdir.

ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r2.speaker: Sıhâh-ı Cevherî
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r2.claim: The lexicon glosses demdeme as sticking something to the ground and crushing it by rubbing.
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r2.anchor: Sıhâh-ı Cevherî’de der ki: دَمْدَمْتُ الشَّيْءَ أَلْزَقـْتُهُ بِالأَْرْضِ

ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r3.speaker: Kāmûs
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r3.claim: The lexicon explains the verb as grinding a people and destroying them; it also carries wrath and angry growling speech.
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r3.anchor: Kāmûs’ta دَمْدَمَ الْقَوْمَ وَدَمْدَمَ عَلَيْهِمْ طَحَنـَهُمْ فَأَهْلَكَهُمْ

ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r4.speaker: Müfessirîn
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r4.claim: Exegetes understand the repeated coating as bringing sins down upon the people through wrathful punishment, annihilating them completely.
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r4.anchor: Müfessirîn burada başlıca mükerrer sıvama ve kabri tamamen bastırma mânasından

ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r5.claim: The pronoun in fasawwāhā may refer to the punishment, making it cover everyone equally, or to the earth, which was flattened over their dwellings.
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r5.anchor: فَسَوَّىٰهَا’daki هَا zamirinin de işaret ettiğimiz vechile “demdeme” masdarına veya

ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r6.claim: He finds the pronoun's return to demdeme more apparent, fitting the preceding feminine noun and the image of total punishment.
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r6.anchor: “Demdeme”ye rücû‘u daha zâhir ve şu zamire de muvâfıktır

ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r10.claim: God's annihilation of the guilty is neither harm to Himself nor injustice to them: He created them and can restore or recompense them, so His judgment is pure justice.
ELMALILI:91:11-15#2/r10.anchor: O helâk ettiği mahlûkātın daha iyisini yaratmaya ve helâklerinden sonra da onlara dilediği sevab

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r1.claim: Q 91, 89, and 85 contain three Group II allusions to Thamud, Ad, and Pharaoh; alongside Q 105, they are the earliest narrative Quranic texts and the nucleus of later punishment legends.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Der Abschnitt gehört zu den insgesamt drei Passagen in Gruppe II der frühmekkanischen Suren, in denen Anspielungen auf die Ṯamūd, die ʿĀd und auf Pharao begegnen

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r2.claim: The fullest other early-Makkan Thamud account is later Q 54:23–31; shorter allusions also occur in 89, 69, and 51, while Q 85 and 89 connect the story to Pharaoh and Ad.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Eine relativ ausführliche Darstellung der Ṯamūd-Legende findet sich in frühmekkanischer Zeit nur noch in der sicherlich später als Q 91 anzusetzenden Passage 54:23–31

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r3.claim: Umayya b. Abi al-Salt’s likely authentic poem lacks a divine warner and explicit command; the camel’s foal’s curse triggers destruction, and its named culprit Aḥmar is elsewhere associated with Ad, perhaps showing tribal names or traditions overlapped.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Es fehlt die Figur eines göttlich gesandten Warners, dessen expliziten Anweisungen die Ṯamūd zuwider handeln, und ihre Vernichtung wird durch einen Fluch ausgelöst

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:14:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:14:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:14:anmerkung/r1.claim: The long verse can be divided after ʿaqarūhā, as in the Himṣ, Mecca b, and Medina I traditions; this matches the offense/punishment break and rhyme, though Himṣ lacks an ending after sawwāhā, where rhyme requires a division.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:14:anmerkung/r1.anchor: V. 14 wirkt überlang, lässt sich jedoch nach ʿaqarūhā in zwei Einzelverse unterteilen, wie dies auch Ḥimṣ, Mekka b und Medina I tun

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:14:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:14:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:14:anmerkung/r2.claim: For the different uses of kaḏḏaba, consult notes at 95:7, 92:16, and 73:11.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:14:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Zu den verschiedenen Gebrauchsweisen von kaḏḏaba vgl. die Anmerkungen zu 95:7, 92:16 und 73:11.

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:14:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:14:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:14:anmerkung/r3.claim: Damdama likely derives from damma, ‘level the ground’ or ‘strike’; traditional senses ‘be angry’ and ‘punish’ seem inferred from the verse, so damdama ʿalaihim is probably synonymous with sawwā.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:14:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Damdama ist wohl von damma abzuleiten, was u. a. „den Erdboden einebnen“ und „schlagen“ bedeutet

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r1.claim: This is the oldest genuine Quranic punishment legend: it recasts the likely pre-Islamic Thamud story as an example of the choice between good and evil and may mirror the Quranic preacher’s rejection by hearers.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r1.anchor: Die vorliegende Sure funktionalisiert die sicherlich bereits in vorkoranischer Zeit bekannte Ṯamūd-Legende als historisches Exempel für die Konsequenzen der zuvor formulierten Alternative von Gut und Böse

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r2.claim: Compared with Umayya’s poem, the Quran adds a divine messenger and an explicit command to spare the camel; the pre-Islamic offense was cultic disrespect toward a consecrated camel, so the Quran theologically reconfigures the inherited story.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r2.anchor: Das Vergehen der Ṯamūd wird bei Umayya als ein Kultfrevel geschildert, als Mißachtung der Unverletzlichkeit eines geweihten Kamels, nicht als Übertretung eines – durch einen prophetischen Boten überbrachten – göttlichen Verbots.

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r4.claim: The passage foregrounds ethical judgment rather than description: it calls Thamud deniers and rebels in verse 11, then repeats kadhdhaba in verse 14 to make rejection of the messenger the immediate cause of destruction; the term may reflect Syriac kaddeb.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r4.anchor: Ein zweites Mal erscheint das Verb kaḏḏaba – das offenbar bereits terminologischen Status hat und wohl mit syr. kaddeb in Verbindung zu bringen ist

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r5.claim: The Quran omits Umayya’s aftermath in which a lame servant survives, reports the event, and dies, since that addition does not serve the general lesson.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r5.anchor: Die theologische Zuspitzung der koranischen Version wird überdies daran sichtbar, dass hier das bei Umayya erzählte Nachspiel

CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r6.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r6.claim: Sawwā describes God’s creative formation of the soul in verse 7 and leveling in punishment in verse 14; the double use is sarcastic and links creation’s moral obligation to judgment’s enforcement of it.
CORPUSCORANICUM:91:11-15:kommentar/r6.anchor: Die Sure charakterisiert also sowohl Gottes kreative Schöpfertätigkeit als auch seine destruktive Straftätigkeit mit demselben Verb.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:11/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:11/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:11/r1.claim: The account of Thamud exemplifies a community's wrong choice after humans were given the ability to choose good or evil; its destruction is a warning, as in the accounts in al-A'raf and Hud.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:11/r1.anchor: Semûd kavminin yanlış seçimi ve bu yüzden başlarına gelen büyük felâket

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:11/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:11/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:11/r2.claim: The camel's slaughter alone did not cause the disaster: it was punishment for denying Salih's prophethood, calling him a liar, and persisting in evil.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:91:11/r2.anchor: felâket, 14. âyette belirtilen “tekzib”in yani Allah’ın elçisi Salih’i peygamber olarak tanımayıp

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p372#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p372#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p372#2/r2.claim: For ولا يخاف عقباها, wāw starts a new sentence after فسواها because the fear is not their act; faʾ instead links the clauses in ordered sequence.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p372#2/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ ولا يخاف عقباها ﴾ يقرأ بالواو والفاء فالحجة لمن قرأه بالواو

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p372#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p372#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p372#2/r3.claim: The fāʾ reading presents the ending as sequential; Ibn Khālawayh glosses فدمدم as ‘destroyed,’ فسواها as making their homes graves, and عقباها as the outcome of its affair.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p372#2/r3.anchor: ومعنى قوله فدمدم أي فهدم ومعنى فسواها أي سوى بيوتهم قبورهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r1.claim: They denied Ṣāliḥ's threat, which could refer to the warning against touching the camel or to the warning implied by his command; another reading has him explicitly relay God's command.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r1.anchor: فكذبوه أي في وعيده إياهم كما حكى عنه بقوله تعالى ولا تمسوها بسوء فيأخذكم عذاب أليم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r2.claim: They hamstrung or slaughtered her; the plural can describe the single culprit because the people all approved his act.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r2.anchor: فعقروها أي فنحروها أو أو فقتلوها وضمير الجمع للأشقى وجمعه على تقدير وحدته لرضا الكل بفعله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r3.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r3.claim: Qatāda says the people, young and old, male and female, all joined the act before it was done.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r3.anchor: قال قتادة بلغنا أنه لم يعقرها حتى تابعه صغيرهم وكبيرهم وذكرهم وأنثاهم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r4.claim: Damdama means that punishment enveloped them; lexicographers also gloss it as completing punishment, sticking something to earth and crushing it, or exterminating utterly. Ibn al-Zubayr has a variant with two dāl consonants.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r4.anchor: فدمدم عليهم ربهم فأطبق عليهم العذاب وقالوا دمدم عليه القبر أي أطبقه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r5.claim: The phrase 'because of their sin' makes the cause explicit to warn every sinner; 'made it even' means none escaped, whether the pronoun refers to the punishment or the tribe, or that the tribe was levelled to earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p145#3/r5.anchor: بذنبهم بسبب ذنبهم المحكي والتصريح بذلك مع دلالة الفاء عليه للأنذار بعاقبة الذنب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440/r5.claim: They rejected Salih and hamstrung the she-camel.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440#2/r1.speaker: عطاء ومقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440#2/r1.claim: Ata and Muqatil gloss damdama as God destroying them; al-Muʾarrij specifies total annihilation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440#2/r1.anchor: قال عطاء ومقاتل: فدمر عليهم ربهم فأهلكهم. قال المؤرج: الدمدمة إهلاك باستئصال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440#2/r2.claim: Their sin was denying the messenger and hamstringing the camel; God leveled punishment over all, leaving no one alive.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440#2/r2.anchor: بتكذيبهم الرسول وعقرهم الناقة، {فسواها} فسوى الدمدمة عليهم جميعا، وعمهم بها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440#2/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ says the whole nation was leveled, with punishment falling on young and old alike.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p440#2/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء: سوى الأمة وأنزل العذاب بصغيرها وكبيرها، يعني سوى بينهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r4.claim: They rejected the warning, hamstrung her, and God overwhelmed them with punishment for their sin; دمدم evokes layering the people with punishment.
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r4.anchor: فأطبق عليهم العذاب وهو من تكرير قولهم ناقة مدمومة إذا ألبسها الشحم

BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r5.claim: God made the punishment uniform so no young or old escaped, or annihilated all Thamūd.
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r5.anchor: فسوى الدمدمة بينهم أو عليهم فلم يفلت منهم صغير ولا كبير

BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r7.claim: A report says reciting al-Shams is like giving charity over everything illuminated by the sun and moon.
BAYDAWI-FULL:91:12-15/r7.anchor: من قرأ سورة والشمس فكأنما تصدق بكل شيء طلعت عليه الشمس والقمر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r8.claim: Some killed the camel directly and others by consent, so the whole people shared in the denial and crime.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r8.anchor: بسبب ذلك التكذيب بعضهم بالفعل وبعضهم بالرضا به

BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r9.speaker: الرازي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r9.claim: Al-Rāzī explains damdama as shaking a structure until it topples.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r10.claim: Damdama was a total, covering, annihilating punishment; the wording indicates its severity and encirclement, while rabbihim recalls the benefactor they rejected.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r10.anchor: عذب عذابا تاما مجللا مغطيا مطبقا مستأصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r11.claim: The punishment leveled strong and weak together, killing everyone at once because the people shared complicity in the camel's killing.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r11.anchor: فكانت الدمدمة على قويهم كما كانت على ضعيفهم

BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r12.claim: The camel allegorically represents the soul as a mount through life's trials, and its water represents remembrance and worship; neglecting these gifts is like slaughtering it.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p442/r12.anchor: فإن الناقة عبارة عن مطية يقطع عليها السير حسا أو معنى

DURR-FULL:v8p530/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r2.claim: He reports that young and old, men and women, all joined in the camel's slaughter, so God destroyed them for their shared sin and feared no consequence.
DURR-FULL:v8p530/r2.anchor: ذكر لنا أنه أبى أن يعقرها حتى تابعه صغيرهم وكبيرهم وذكرهم وأنثاهم فلما اشترك القوم في عقرها

TAB:91:14/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:14/r1.speaker: author
TAB:91:14/r1.claim: They rejected Salih's report that God assigned the she-camel a drinking day and would punish them if they hamstrung her.
TAB:91:14/r1.anchor: فكذبوا صالحا في خبره الذي أخبرهم به

TAB:91:14/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:14/r2.speaker: author
TAB:91:14/r2.claim: The denial may itself refer to hamstringing the she-camel.
TAB:91:14/r2.anchor: وقد يحتمل أن يكون التكذيب بالعقر

TAB:91:14/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:14/r3.speaker: author
TAB:91:14/r3.claim: Because denial and hamstringing were connected actions, either may be mentioned first, as giving and doing good can be ordered either way.

TAB:91:14/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:14/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB:91:14/r4.claim: Some treat ‘they denied him’ as a complete clause and make ‘they hamstrung it’ the response to 91:12, when the most wretched arose.
TAB:91:14/r4.anchor: بعضهم أن قوله : فكذبوه كلمة مكتفية بنفسها

TAB:91:14/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:14/r5.speaker: author
TAB:91:14/r5.claim: Although they had accepted alternating drinking days, all agreed to deny the she-camel water and consented to her killing, so the acts are attributed to the whole people.

TAB:91:14/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:14/r6.speaker: author
TAB:91:14/r6.claim: God destroyed them for their sin, their denial of Salih, and their hamstringing of the she-camel, leveling the punishment over all so none escaped.
TAB:91:14/r6.anchor: الدمدمة عليهم جميعهم ،   فلم يفلت منهم أحد

TAB:91:14/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:14/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB:91:14/r7.claim: Qatada reports that Thamud's red-haired man would not hamstring the she-camel until all, young and old, male and female, pledged with him; God then punished them all.
TAB:91:14/r7.anchor: عن قتادة ،   قوله :  فدمدم عليهم ربهم

TAB:91:14/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:91:14/r8.speaker: الحسن
TAB:91:14/r8.claim: Al-Hasan says that after hamstringing the she-camel, they pursued her calf; it fled to a mountain crag, and God struck their hearts.
TAB:91:14/r8.anchor: سمعت الحسن يقول :  لما عقروا الناقة طلبوا فصيلها

BURHAN:v3p279/r14.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p279/r14.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p279/r14.claim: The people first hamstrung the she-camel, then denied him concerning both the hamstringing and their response.
BURHAN:v3p279/r14.anchor: أي فعقروها ثم كذبوه في عقرها وفي إجابتهم

ITQAN:v3p243/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p243/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p243/r1.claim: Good ordering presents a subject’s attributes in their natural order without adding an extra trait; al-Yamani illustrates it with human development and with the people first rejecting Salih, then hamstringing the she-camel.
ITQAN:v3p243/r1.anchor: هو أن يورد أوصاف الموصوف على ترتيبها في الخلقة الطبيعية ولا يدخل فيها وصفا زائدا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r8.claim: The sequence can be read with hamstringing first: their act of hamstringing the she-camel was their denial of Salih’s claim.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r9.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r9.claim: Alternatively, they denied Salih’s statement that it was God’s she-camel, then hamstrung it.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r9.anchor: وقد يجوز أن يكون أراد: فكذبوا قوله: إنها ناقة الله، فعقروها

ABUHAYYAN:91:14/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:14/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:91:14/r1.claim: Damdama al-qabr means to cover or seal it.
ABUHAYYAN:91:14/r1.anchor: دمدم عليه القبر : أطبقه .   وقال مؤرج : الدمدمة : إهلاك باستئصال .

ABUHAYYAN:91:14/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:14/r2.speaker: مؤرج
ABUHAYYAN:91:14/r2.claim: Muʾarrij defines damdama as destruction that annihilates completely.
ABUHAYYAN:91:14/r2.anchor: وقال مؤرج : الدمدمة : إهلاك باستئصال .   وقال في الصحاح : دمدمت الشيء

ABUHAYYAN:91:14/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:14/r3.speaker: الصحاح
ABUHAYYAN:91:14/r3.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ glosses the verb as pressing something to the ground and crushing it.
ABUHAYYAN:91:14/r3.anchor: وقال في الصحاح : دمدمت الشيء : ألزقته بالأرض وطحطحته .

ABUHAYYAN:91:14/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:91:14/r4.speaker: الجمهور وقيل
